title: Drop the rise in machine games duty
name: Drop the rise in machine games duty
noun: dropping the machine games duty rise
headline: Drop machine games rise. Costs £0.1bn in 2029-30.
description: Duty on higher-stake gaming machines rises from 20% to 25% from April 2027, and from April 2028 the machine’s supplier pays it. Switch this on to drop both.

baselinePolicy.text: Machine games duty is 25% on higher-stake machines from 1 April 2027, paid by the supplier from 1 April 2028 (Table 6.1 line 56).

source.quote: This measure increases the Machine Games Duty rate from 20% to 25% on machines with a maximum stake above £1 or a maximum prize above £100.

alreadyIncludes: Machine games duty is 25% on higher-stake machines from 1 April 2027, paid by the supplier from 1 April 2028 (Table 6.1 line 56).

lines.title: Machine Games Duty: Increase the rate from 20% to 25% for higher stake machines from 1 April 2027 and move duty liability to the machine supplier from 1 April 2028

rawSource.note: Reversal: the Treasury’s costing with its sign reversed (positive scorecard values reduce borrowing; here receipts positive means more revenue).

caveats: The Treasury’s costing is on the OBR October 2026 forecast, the baseline used here. Effects before the start year are not applied: 2026-27 falls before any Budget of yours.

considerations.text: The Treasury’s scorecard figure is the certified direct costing for the measure, including the behavioural response the Treasury and OBR agreed; the Budget 2026 policy costings document gives the method.
